blockers.quote: Google has offered to suggest your replies since 2015, and to finish your sentences since 2018 (c11).
blockers.why: Claim c11's verbatim quotes and source URLs apply specifically to email ('writes email', 'complete sentences in your emails'). Stating 'suggest your replies' and 'finish your sentences' in a scene showing phone chat messages overstates the scope of what Google offered in 2015 and 2018 to general messaging.
blockers.fix: Google has offered to suggest your replies in email since 2015, and to finish your sentences since 2018 (c11).

blockers.quote: Around the turn of the century, the Philippines was called the texting capital of the world (c01). By 2008: over a billion texts a day (c02).
blockers.why: Claim c02's verbatim quote specifically measures volume in the Philippines ('the Philippines alone sent, on average, over 1 billion text messages a day'). Omitting geographic scope wording ('there') leaves the daily volume unbounded and overstates general text volume.
blockers.fix: Around the turn of the century, the Philippines was called the texting capital of the world (c01). By 2008: over a billion texts a day there (c02).

keep.quote: One security company estimated that in 2024, bots, good and bad, passed people: 51 per cent of all web traffic, for the first time in a decade (c09).
Your father is one of about two million Filipinos working overseas (c04). For a family like yours, the phone is where home is.

In a 2023 study, people who suspected their chat partner was using AI-suggested replies judged them more harshly (c22). But actually using them made the conversation warmer and closer (c22). The use never hurt the conversation. The suspicion did.
